page: Amazon Web Services m8i.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The processor is an Intel Xeon 6975P-C running at 3.9 GHz, equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. It includes 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and image processing scores placing in the top 10% tier. The server also achieves top-tier performance in static web serving throughput and prompt processing for medium and large language models. Memory bandwidth for cached read-only operations is strong, though large-block uncached memory writes and large-model text generation fall into the average tier. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for enterprise workloads that require high-speed DDR5 memory and strong multi-core compute capabilities without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The absence of local storage means storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. This server is well-suited for workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
